claims.statement: EodhdPriceRepository is the only registered PriceRepository and works read-through: get_prices reads the DB range, fetches the same range from EODHD, and persists the union with EODHD rows winning per date; get_latest_price only refetches when the stored close predates the last expected NYSE trading day (weekends and holidays.NYSE() skipped); get_price_on_date falls back to EODHD and saves the result; save_price/save_prices raise NotImplementedError so writes must go through the inner DB repository or MarketService.

EodhdGateway is the sole EODHD integration point, builds symbols as `{symbol}.{exchange}`, uses the eodhd APIClient for historical data and a raw requests.get for the search endpoint, drops flat zero-volume candles, supports only the '1h' intraday interval (raising ValueError otherwise), and is swapped for StubEodhdGateway when settings.stub_external_api is set.

GET /market/prices/{security_id} requires from_date and to_date (422 otherwise) for 1d/1w/1m and derives weekly/monthly candles in-process via aggregate_weekly_prices and aggregate_monthly_prices; for intraday intervals it reads IntradayPriceRepository and triggers an on-demand backfill through MarketService.fetch_and_save_intraday_prices when the result is empty or its first candle starts more than 4 days after from_date, then aggregates 4h buckets via aggregate_4h_candles.

Price aggregation is pure and shared: aggregate_weekly_prices groups by ISO (year, week) and aggregate_monthly_prices by (year, month), each taking open from the first candle, close/adjusted_close from the last, max high, min low and summed volume; aggregate_4h_candles buckets hourly candles by hour // 4 with the same contract; all three are re-exposed as static methods on PriceAggregationService.

MarketService.update_daily_prices_for_all_securities fetches all active securities and updates each for the last 365 days in a single asyncio.gather, returning success/failure counts, and _update_security_prices swallows per-security exceptions and returns False so one failing symbol cannot abort the batch; update_intraday_prices_for_all_securities has the same shape over the last 7 days at the '1h' interval; fetch_and_save_price_history backfills from 2000-01-03 and fetch_and_save_intraday_prices defaults to a 30-day window.

Three Huey periodic tasks live in src/market/task.py: daily_price_update at crontab(hour='0', minute='0') and hourly_intraday_price_update at crontab(minute='0') drive price ingestion, and daily_fx_refresh at crontab(hour='17', minute='30') refreshes ECB FX rates into Redis. The price tasks resolve services from huey.svcs_registry inside an svcs Container and raise RuntimeError when the registry is missing, while daily_fx_refresh works directly on redis_manager and a plain httpx.AsyncClient; huey is a MemoryHueyWithRegistry under ENVIRONMENT=test and a RedisHueyWithRegistry otherwise, the registry is attached in the @huey.on_startup hook, and the dev worker runs huey_consumer with --worker-type thread --periodic.

Only the hourly task fans out: after updating intraday prices it performs two isolated enqueues — recalculate_all_account_totals_task and check_and_dispatch_price_alerts — each wrapped in its own try/except so failure to enqueue one cannot abort the other or the task itself.

Stage 2 (check_and_dispatch_price_alerts) returns early without querying intraday prices when there are no untriggered alerts; otherwise it loads one latest-intraday-close-per-security map, delegates to AlertEvaluationService.evaluate (pure static method: 'above' triggers at latest >= target and 'below' at latest <= target, both inclusive; a security with no price is skipped), and enqueues one alert_email_dispatch_task per triggered alert inside a per-alert try/except, threading the Stage 2 run timestamp.

Stage 3 (alert_email_dispatch_task, @huey.task(retries=3)) follows an email-then-mark invariant: it re-fetches the alert and no-ops if missing or already triggered (idempotency guard against retry duplication), re-resolves the latest price at dispatch time instead of reusing the Stage 2 snapshot, resolves the recipient via UserApi.get_email_for_user, sends the email, and only then calls PriceAlertRepository.mark_triggered; a send failure re-raises so Huey retries and leaves triggered_at NULL so the next hourly run re-enqueues the alert.

GET /market/securities/{security_id}/indicators computes a fixed set of indicators in Python from stored daily prices via src/market/indicators.py (50/200-day and 50/200-week MAs, MACD, RSI), reducing to weekly closes first for the weekly variants; it accepts only indicator names with no interval, custom candles or date window, and caches results in Redis.

POST /market/securities/{security_id}/indicators/compute (handler `market_compute_indicators`) validates and normalizes the date/datetime union before comparing bounds (reversed window → 422, avoiding a TypeError from naive/aware comparison), consults the IndicatorCache only when the caller supplied no candles, resolves candles from PriceRepository (daily/weekly/monthly, aggregated per interval, time as a date ISO string) or IntradayPriceRepository (time as integer epoch seconds), applies convert_to_heikin_ashi before dispatch when chart_style is heikin_ashi, calls IndicatorServiceClient.compute, and writes the cache only for the server-resolved path.

IndicatorCache keys are 'indicators:<security_id>:<interval>:<chart_style>:<sha256 digest>' with ':<price_count>' appended when a price count is supplied; the digest hashes a canonical payload of individually json.dumps(sort_keys=True)-serialized specs (strings canonicalized to {"type": …}, models dumped by_alias with exclude_none, dicts passed through), sorted, plus date-only-normalized from_date/to_date — making the key order-insensitive to indicator order but sensitive to interval, chart style and window. The TTL is 3600 seconds via setex, invalidate_security scans and deletes 'indicators:*<security_id>*', flush_all deletes 'indicators:*', and every Redis error degrades to a cache miss or no-op.

SecuritySearchCache uses key 'market:search:<normalized query>' with normalization being strip, lowercase and collapse of internal whitespace, and a DEFAULT_SEARCH_CACHE_TTL of 2_592_000 seconds (30 days) applied via setex, with set accepting a per-call TTL override; a non-list cached payload is treated as a miss. It backs both search endpoints and SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker, so search results are cached far longer than indicator results.

GET /market/search and its alias GET /market/securities/search share one handler that is cache-first against SecuritySearchCache and only calls MarketGateway.search on a miss, then writes the results back; the endpoints require an authenticated user and a query of length 1..100.

The Go indicator sidecar (services/indicator-service) is stateless: POST /compute takes {interval, candles, indicators} with interval defaulting to '1d', returns 200 with an 'indicators' map keyed by each spec's ResultKey (id when set, else type), and returns an empty array rather than an error when there are too few candles; GET /health returns a status payload; other methods get 405 with an Allow header; 400 covers invalid JSON and unsupported indicator types; the body is capped at 10MB via http.MaxBytesReader.

The sidecar has no authentication and no rate limiting and is intended for the internal Docker network only, with the FastAPI backend as its only intended client; it is built on github.com/cinar/indicator/v2, supports sma, ema, bb, macd, rsi, obv and the ma50/ma200/ma50w/ma200w aliases, resolves parameters as top-level field (> 0) → settings map → built-in default, and rescales the ma* periods to the requested interval (e.g. ma50 on 1h becomes a 350-candle SMA) leaving unknown intervals unscaled.

IndicatorServiceClient posts {interval, candles, indicators} to <base_url>/compute with a default 10.0s timeout and maps failures to backend statuses: httpx.TimeoutException → 504 'Indicator service timed out', httpx.ConnectError/NetworkError → 503 'Indicator service unavailable', upstream 400 → 400 with the sidecar's error text as detail, upstream 5xx → 503, and any other non-200 → that status with the response text; on success it unwraps the 'indicators' envelope. It reuses one owned httpx.AsyncClient and closes it on teardown, but never closes an injected client.

settings.indicator_service_url defaults to http://localhost:8080 and is configured through INDICATOR_SERVICE_URL (.env.example sets http://indicator-service:8080 for Compose); dev compose publishes 127.0.0.1:${INDICATOR_SERVICE_PORT:-8004} to container port 8080 while prod compose publishes no host port at all (internal network only, container retail-portfolio-indicator-service, restart always), and both compose files healthcheck GET /health via wget every 30s.

On the frontend, IndicatorsService.computeIndicators(securityId, {interval, chart_style, indicators, candles?, from_date?, to_date?}) targets POST /market/securities/{id}/indicators/compute and its TypeScript indicator types mirror the Pydantic schemas; the security page batches all enabled indicators into one request in refreshActiveIndicators (rendering volume locally and treating avgPrice as a price line rather than a series), sends a single spec per toggle in onIndicatorToggle, and discards stale responses using a monotonic sequenceCounter plus a per-indicator indicatorSeq map, catching and logging errors so a sidecar outage only degrades indicator series.

The chart's rewind feature is why the compute request accepts caller-supplied candles: a rewound request sends the sliced candle array so indicators reflect the values they would have had at that instant, and because the backend only reads or writes the indicator cache when no candles are supplied, that request bypasses caching entirely.

Market-data tests stub both EODHD and the sidecar so no test requires a live external service: test_indicator_client.py drives IndicatorServiceClient through httpx.MockTransport, test_indicator_compute_api.py patches IndicatorServiceClient.compute and IndicatorCache at the router level, test_eodhd.py patches src.market.eodhd.APIClient and exercises the stub gateway directly, and test_search_router.py registers a MagicMock MarketGateway plus an AsyncMock SecuritySearchCache on the app's svcs registry; the Go sidecar is covered offline by internal/indicators/{calculator_test.go,timeframe_test.go}, internal/httpapi/{handlers_test.go,middleware_test.go}, internal/config/config_test.go and internal/logging/logger_test.go via go test ./... .

src/commands/flush_market_data.py is the operational escape hatch for market data: --security-id deletes that security's PriceModel and IntradayPriceModel rows and calls IndicatorCache.invalidate_security, --all deletes both tables and calls IndicatorCache.flush_all, and both print row counts and require interactive confirmation.

POST /market/securities/{security_id}/indicators/compute is implemented by `market_compute_indicators` in src/market/router.py: it takes IndicatorComputeRequest (interval default 1d, chart_style, IndicatorSpecSchema list, optional candles, optional from/to bounds) and IndicatorComputeResponse carries a single `indicators: dict[str, Any]` map, so the route returns series keyed by each spec's sidecar ResultKey rather than by fixed Pydantic fields. The sibling GET /market/securities/{security_id}/indicators is a different handler (`market_get_technical_indicators`) hidden behind the same path prefix.

The in-process endpoint GET /market/securities/{security_id}/indicators accepts only a repeatable `indicators` query parameter of indicator names and always computes over the security's full stored history (PriceRepository.get_by_security — a pure DB read that never calls EODHD); it has no interval, chart style, custom-candle or date-window input, returns an empty TechnicalIndicatorsRead when no prices exist, and only recognises the six fixed names ma_50_day, ma_200_day, ma_50_week, ma_200_week, macd and rsi. It caches both the read and the write through IndicatorCache with price_count = len(prices), so a cache hit short-circuits before any computation and a growing history naturally misses.

For the daily/weekly/monthly branch of the compute route, each stored price is converted to a split-adjusted candle before dispatch: split_ratio is adjusted_close / close when adjusted_close is present, non-zero-denominator and different from close, otherwise 1.0; open/high/low are multiplied by that ratio and close is taken directly from adjusted_close when a split is detected. Volume is passed through unadjusted.

The intraday branch of the compute route converts the optional date/datetime bounds into a UTC datetime range via `_to_datetime_range` — a bare `date` becomes datetime.combine(date, time.min) for the lower bound and time.max for the upper bound, naive datetimes are stamped with UTC, and tz-aware datetimes pass through — which is what makes the intraday repository read well-defined when callers send date-only strings.

IndicatorCache is used defensively by both indicator paths: every Redis get, set, invalidate and flush is wrapped in a broad try/except that logs a warning and degrades to a miss or a no-op. A cache outage therefore never fails an indicator request — it only costs a recomputation — which is the opposite of the sidecar failure mode, where IndicatorServiceClient raises HTTPException 503/504 up through the route. On the frontend the resulting error is caught and logged, leaving the chart without indicator series rather than breaking the page.

The frontend rewind path is what produces caller-supplied candles: `getRewoundCandlesPayload` returns undefined unless the chart is rewound and a timeline position exists, and otherwise slices the raw candles up to that position into the request's `candles` array. Both the batched `refreshActiveIndicators` and the single-spec `onIndicatorToggle` attach that payload when it is present, and both resolve each returned series under the spec `id` first and its `type` second, matching the sidecar's ResultKey rule.

Price alerts are managed by three per-user, paginated market_router handlers — market_get_alerts (GET), market_create_alert (POST) and market_delete_alert (DELETE …/alerts/{alert_id}) — over PriceAlertRepository.get_by_security_and_user / create / delete, which is the CRUD surface that produces the alerts the hourly cascade evaluates; PriceAlertRepository also exposes the evaluation-facing get_active_alerts_for_evaluation, mark_triggered and get_by_id used by Stages 2 and 3.

A new indicator type is an extension boundary of the Go sidecar, not of Python: the sidecar's type switch in calculator.go is the single dispatch point for supported types (defaulting to an "unsupported indicator type" error), so a type added to src/market/indicators.py would only ever be reachable from the legacy in-process endpoint and would be invisible to the chart's compute route.

Tests for the compute route patch IndicatorServiceClient.compute and IndicatorCache's get/set at the router level — never a live sidecar — and test_indicator_client.py drives the real client through httpx.MockTransport; this is possible because IndicatorServiceClient only closes a client it created itself, leaving an injected transport-backed client intact.

The market domain binds two svcs keys over the same MarketGateway ABC: MarketGateway resolves eodhd_gateway_factory (EODHD) and serves the in-app price flows — EodhdPriceRepository, MarketService and the /market/search routes — while DataPlaneMarketGateway resolves composite_market_gateway_factory (a CompositeMarketGateway routing prices, search, fundamentals and quotes to FMP and options to Polygon) and serves src/market/data_router.py plus the user-facing GET /market/securities/{security_id}/institutional-ownership route; both keys are registered in the live and stub registries, so stub_external_api swaps the providers but never the key layout.

GET /market/securities/{security_id}/institutional-ownership is the only user-JWT market read served by DataPlaneMarketGateway: it caches the response under 'market:institutional_ownership:<security_id>' for 86_400 seconds, degrades both MarketDataNotFoundError and MarketDataProviderError to a null-valued, empty-history response, caches only the not-found case, and treats Redis read/write failures as warnings so the endpoint still answers from the provider.

GET /market/logo and GET /market/securities/{security_id}/logo are the only routes on market_router without a current_user dependency; both map the symbol with map_to_fmp_ticker, fetch the PNG through FMP's fetch_logo_image, and cache raw bytes in LogoCache under 'market:logo:<TICKER>' for 30 days with a one-day '__not_found__' sentinel that yields 404 without re-querying FMP, serving successes with Cache-Control public, max-age=604800.

POST /compute validates fixed request bounds before computing anything and rejects violations with 400: at most 32 indicators, at most 50,000 candles, resolved period/fast/slow/signal within [1, 1000] and resolved stdDev within (0, 10], with each error message naming the offending field and the indicator's ResultKey.

The sidecar's output contract echoes each input candle's `time` untouched, drops NaN/Inf points so a series may start after the first candle, and varies the point shape by family ({time,value} for SMA/EMA/OBV, {time,middle,upper,lower} for Bollinger, {time,macd,signal,histogram} for MACD, {time,value,rsi} for RSI); its canonical type names (ma50, ma200, ma50w, ma200w, bb, macd, rsi, obv) are exactly the chart's indicator ids, so the chart never depends on the alias families.

The compute route resolves the security only on the server-resolved candle path: a request that supplies its own `candles` never touches the security, price or intraday repositories, so it returns 200 even for an unknown security_id, whereas the same request without candles fails with 404.
